## Principle

The test/train split and the CV folds are **one problem**, not two. Pili et al.
(2025) report internal CV with no stated holdout. CAST (`geodist`/`knndm`) gives
a prediction-matched holdout *or* a fold diagnostic, but not one object that
derives both. Here the partition is a single artifact. Its:

- **unit** is the *connected component* (a graph of nearby points), not an
  arbitrary `k`;
- **separation** is measured on **two axes** — geography (leakage) and
  environment (coverage) — kept apart because the cases where they *decouple*
  are the ecologically interesting ones;
- **split and fold rules** depend on `purpose ∈ {discovery, mapping,
  projection}`. "Can this cluster be split?" is a property of the question, not
  the cluster.

The failure this avoids: on bimodal, clustered rare-plant data, both
E-clustering (collapse a cluster to one point) and vanilla LOPO/NNDM (hold a
whole cluster out) destroy the within-condition replication a sparse endemic
needs. We want clusters **cut and re-represented** for *mapping*, held out
intact for *discovery*.

We build it piecewise. Every step emits its object **and** a plot, so we see
the graphs before anything is folded into a function. The `partition_*` helpers
compose into `build_partition()` at the end.

## Parameters

Everything tunable lives here so the rest of the document is logic, not knobs.

```{r params}
params_part <- list(
  resolution     = 90,            # nominal res for the env stack (90/30/10/3 -> dem_3arc/1arc/1-3arc/3m)
  connect_m      = 500,           # Step 1 graph edge threshold (metres). Derived/justified in Step 1.
  superclust_m   = 40000,         # Step 2a super-cluster cut (metres), inside the 30-75 km gap
  train_target   = c(0.70, 0.80), # Step 4 outer test-holdout: soft train-proportion window
  k              = 10,            # Step 5 inner CV folds (each validates ~1/k of training); CAST's `k`
  purpose        = "mapping",     # discovery | mapping | projection
  pca_var_target = 0.90,          # retain enough env PCA axes to reach this cumulative variance
  min_split_n    = 12,            # Step 3: min presences for a component to be worth cutting
  extrap_frac    = 0.8,           # Step 3: a segment whose whole-holdout puts >= this fraction of its
                                  #   points beyond rest-of-data env-NN p95 is an EXTRAPOLATION segment:
                                  #   kept out of training and its points spread across the holdouts
  seed           = 1021
)
set.seed(params_part$seed)
```

## Setup

This document runs from the **repository root** (`knitr$opts_knit$root.dir` in
the YAML), so every path is root-relative. We source `functions.R` for
`rastReader()`, `res_string()`, etc. Its `PROJ_ROOT` is the data-machine path;
the raster probe below also checks a local `data/spatial/processed` and uses
whichever holds the stack.

```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(terra)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(CAST)   # geodist/knndm/nndm vocabulary; trainDI/aoa (DI + AOA) used in Steps 3-5
})
# distances via FNN and the W statistic via twosamples — the same leaf functions CAST calls
# internally (so these pieces are wraps, not reimplementations); referenced with ::
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  requireNamespace("FNN"); requireNamespace("twosamples")
})

source("scripts/functions.R")  # defines PROJ_ROOT (data-machine), rastReader, res_string, ...

p2dat   <- "data/Data4modelling"
# raster stack may live under the data-machine root or locally; Step 0 probes both
p2proc_candidates <- c(
  file.path(PROJ_ROOT, "data", "spatial", "processed"),
  "data/spatial/processed"
)
```

## Step 0 — Points, populations, and the environmental space

The **presences are the graph unit**, so they drive Steps 1–2. We load the
collated iter2 set (`3m-presence-iter2.gpkg`), which folds the **2026 field
records** into the iter1 presences; `source` keeps provenance so the 2026 points
show on every plot. Background **absences** (`iter1-pa.gpkg`) are loaded aside
here and only enter the class-aware Step 6. We then extract predictors and
reduce to a PCA env space. Without the raster stack, Steps 1–2 run on geography
alone.

```{r step0-points}
# presences: iter2 collated set (iter1 + 2026 field data). Occurrence = 1.
# keep point_id to join the pre-extracted predictor CSV in step0-env.
pts <- st_read(file.path(p2dat, "3m-presence-iter2.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  transmute(Occurrence = 1L, point_id = as.character(point_id),
            source = as.character(source), site = as.character(site),
            .id = row_number())

# background absences, held aside for the class-aware split/folds (Steps 4–5).
bg <- st_read(file.path(p2dat, "iter1-pa.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  transmute(Occurrence = 0L, source = "iter1-pa", site = NA_character_)

cat(nrow(pts), "presences (",
    paste(sprintf("%s: %d", names(table(pts$source)), table(pts$source)), collapse = ", "),
    ") +", nrow(bg), "background absences\n")
```

```{r step0-env}
# Attach environmental predictors + PCA scores. Prefer the pre-extracted CSV
# (point_id join — no rasters needed on this machine); fall back to on-the-fly
# raster extraction if the stack is mounted; else Steps 1–2 run on geography alone.
pred_csv <- file.path(p2dat, "3m-presence-iter2-10m-predictors.csv")
res_str  <- res_string(params_part$resolution)
p2proc   <- p2proc_candidates[file.exists(file.path(p2proc_candidates, paste0("dem_", res_str)))][1]
coord_cols <- c("point_id", "source", "date", "site", "X", "Y", "Longitude", "Latitude")

env <- NULL
if (file.exists(pred_csv)) {
  preds <- readr::read_csv(pred_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(point_id = as.character(point_id))
  env_vars <- setdiff(names(preds)[vapply(preds, is.numeric, logical(1))], coord_cols)
  env <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(point_id) |>
    left_join(select(preds, point_id, all_of(env_vars)), by = "point_id") |>
    select(all_of(env_vars))
  message("Predictors from CSV (", length(env_vars), " vars, point_id join).")
} else if (!is.na(p2proc)) {
  rast_dat <- rastReader(paste0("dem_", res_str), p2proc)
  env <- terra::extract(rast_dat, pts, ID = FALSE)
  env <- env[, vapply(env, is.numeric, logical(1)), drop = FALSE]
  message("Predictors from raster stack at ", p2proc, " (", ncol(env), " vars).")
}

env_ok <- !is.null(env)
if (env_ok) {
  cc     <- complete.cases(env)
  pca    <- prcomp(env[cc, ], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  # retain enough axes to reach the cumulative-variance target (data-driven, not fixed)
  cumvar <- summary(pca)$importance[3, ]
  n_pca  <- as.integer(which(cumvar >= params_part$pca_var_target)[1])
  scores <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(env), n_pca,
                   dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("PC", seq_len(n_pca))))
  scores[cc, ] <- predict(pca, env[cc, ])[, seq_len(n_pca)]
  pts <- bind_cols(pts, as_tibble(scores))
  cat(sprintf("PCA env space: %d axes for %.0f%% variance (%.1f%% achieved); %d presences missing predictors.\n",
              n_pca, 100 * params_part$pca_var_target, 100 * cumvar[n_pca], sum(!cc)))
} else {
  message("No predictors available; Steps 1–2 run on geography alone.")
}
```

```{r step0-plot}
if (env_ok) {
  ggplot(pts, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = source)) +
    geom_point(alpha = .8, size = 1.8) +
    labs(title = "Step 0 — environmental (PCA) space, by source", colour = "source") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

## Step 1 — Graph construction (connected components in geographic space)

Connect any two points within `connect_m`. The connected components of that
graph are our units — the analog of `knndm()$clusters`, but built single-linkage
from a distance graph rather than by `knndm()`'s `ward.D2` hierarchical cut:
single-linkage respects the real gaps in irregular, bimodal data, where Ward
would balance cluster sizes across them. A dense population becomes one component
we can later split; an isolated outlier becomes its own singleton.

### Deriving the threshold (don't trust the round number)

`connect_m` is the master knob: it decides whether two nearby populations are
one component or two. Don't default it. Look at the presence-to-presence
nearest-neighbour distances and set the threshold at the gap between
within-population and between-population scales. (On the data machine, also
check `CAST::geodist()`'s sample-to-prediction distances — the knee there is
the principled choice.)

```{r step1-threshold}
# pts are all presences; NN distance between each presence and its nearest other
nn_m <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(
  pts, pts[sf::st_nearest_feature(pts), ], by_element = TRUE))

tibble(nn_m = nn_m) |>
  ggplot(aes(nn_m)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = params_part$connect_m, colour = "red", linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Step 1 — presence NN-distance distribution (red = chosen connect_m)",
       x = "nearest-neighbour distance (m, log10)", y = "count") +
  theme_minimal()

quantile(nn_m, c(.5, .75, .9, .95, .99)) |> round(1)
```

### Build components

```{r step1-graph}
partition_components <- function(x, connect_m) {
  # Connected components of the within-connect_m graph are identical to single-linkage clusters
  # cut at height connect_m (single-linkage = transitive closure of <=connect_m edges; verified
  # bit-for-bit on these data). Use stats::hclust so the clustering matches CAST's idiom and
  # carries no igraph dependency; the super-cluster step (Step 2a) already uses the same call.
  within <- sf::st_is_within_distance(x, dist = connect_m)  # sparse list kept for the edge plot
  d      <- sf::st_distance(x); units(d) <- NULL
  memb   <- stats::cutree(stats::hclust(stats::as.dist(d), method = "single"), h = connect_m)
  x$component <- factor(memb)
  attr(x, "adj") <- within   # keep for edge plotting / hull distances
  x
}

pts <- partition_components(pts, params_part$connect_m)
cat("components:", nlevels(pts$component),
    "| sizes:", paste(sort(table(pts$component), decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(8, nlevels(pts$component))],
                      collapse = ", "), "...\n")
```

```{r step1-plot}
# edge list from the sparse within-distance object (small n, cheap)
adj   <- attr(pts, "adj")
co    <- sf::st_coordinates(pts)
edges <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(adj), function(i) {
  j <- adj[[i]][adj[[i]] > i]
  if (length(j)) cbind(x = co[i, 1], y = co[i, 2], xend = co[j, 1], yend = co[j, 2]) else NULL
})) |> as.data.frame()

ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               colour = "grey70", linewidth = .3) +
  geom_sf(data = pts, aes(colour = component), size = 1.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Step 1 — %d components (connect_m = %d m)",
                       nlevels(pts$component), params_part$connect_m)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Step 2 — Inter-component geographic distance (minimum, hull-cheapened)

Leakage is about the *closest* points between components, so we want the
**minimum** between-component distance, not centroid distance. Collapsing each
component to a MULTIPOINT and taking `st_distance` gives the exact pairwise
minima. For large components, the convex-hull shortcut applies (only hull
vertices can carry the minimum).

```{r step2-geo}
partition_geo_dist <- function(x, hull = FALSE) {
  parts <- x |>
    group_by(component) |>
    summarise(do_union = TRUE, .groups = "drop")        # one (MULTI)geometry per component
  if (hull) parts <- st_convex_hull(parts)
  d <- sf::st_distance(parts)                            # min distance between geometries
  units::drop_units(d) -> d
  dimnames(d) <- list(levels(x$component), levels(x$component))
  d
}

geo_d <- partition_geo_dist(pts)
as.data.frame(round(geo_d)) |> head(8)
```

## Step 2a — Inter-component environmental distance + the geo/env decoupling diagnostic

A component's env location is the medoid of its PCA scores (robust to within-
cluster spread). The key diagnostic, **before** any rule, is how geographic and
environmental between-component distances relate. Where `knndm()`/`geodist()`
commit to a single `dist_space` (`"geographical"` *or* `"feature"`), we keep both,
because for this species they decouple. The global Spearman rho is not the whole
story. For this species the scatter is **two clouds and a gap** (a
~30–75 km geographic gap between population super-clusters), non-linear and
strongly heteroscedastic. What matters is the **env spread at small geographic
distance**: if adjacent components span a wide env range, geographic folds will
*not* control env extrapolation, and the two axes must stay separate.

Here `rho ≈ 0.64`, but within ~25 km env distance ranges from ~0 to its maximum,
and the two most spatially extreme components are env-*closer* than mid-range
pairs. Colouring the env ordination by **geographic super-cluster** (a single-
linkage cut across the gap) shows why: at the super-cluster scale geo and env
agree (Cochetopa-south and the eastern outliers are the distinct env mode),
while *within* the northern massif env varies independently of geography. That
is the `purpose` hierarchy — super-cluster = discovery unit, within-super-cluster
= mapping unit.

```{r step2a-env, eval=env_ok}
partition_env_dist <- function(x, pcs) {
  sc <- x |> st_drop_geometry() |> select(component, all_of(pcs))
  medoids <- sc |>
    group_by(component) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(pcs), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
  m <- as.matrix(medoids[, pcs]); rownames(m) <- medoids$component
  as.matrix(dist(m))
}

pcs   <- grep("^PC", names(pts), value = TRUE)
env_d <- partition_env_dist(pts, pcs)

# align and correlate the off-diagonal pairs
ut <- upper.tri(geo_d)
decouple <- tibble(geo_m = geo_d[ut], env_d = env_d[ut])
rho <- cor(decouple$geo_m, decouple$env_d, method = "spearman")

ggplot(decouple, aes(geo_m / 1000, env_d)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .35, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "red", linewidth = .6) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Step 2a — geo vs env between-component distance (Spearman rho = %.2f)", rho),
       x = "min geographic distance (km)", y = "env (PCA medoid) distance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Geographic super-clusters and the env-space view

A single-linkage cut of the component min-distance matrix across the gap
recovers the super-clusters. Colouring the env ordination by them resolves the
structure: a super-cluster that occupies its own env region (geo≈env, a valid
discovery holdout) versus one that smears across env space (geo⊥env, where
mapping needs env-aware folds).

```{r step2a-superclusters, eval=env_ok}
# super-clusters: single-linkage so the cut respects the inter-cluster gap, not centroids
superc <- cutree(hclust(as.dist(geo_d), method = "single"), h = params_part$superclust_m)
pts$supercluster <- factor(superc[as.character(pts$component)])
cat(length(unique(superc)), "geographic super-clusters at a ",
    params_part$superclust_m / 1000, " km cut; component counts:\n")
print(table(superc))

med <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(component, supercluster) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(pcs), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(med, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = supercluster, size = n)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .75) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = component), size = 2.3, max.overlaps = 40,
                           show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 10)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(title = "Step 2a — component medoids in env space, by geographic super-cluster",
       subtitle = "single-linkage cut at 40 km; size = n presences") +
  theme_minimal()
```


---

# Decision-bearing steps

The pieces above are the *inputs*. Steps 3–6 encode the design choices, all for
`purpose = "mapping"` here (discovery/projection branches are stubbed).

## Step 3 — Roles: extrapolation, splittable, atomic

Each component gets one role, and the role drives how Steps 4–6 allocate it. The
decision rests on one **realized** measure: hold a component out *whole*, and ask
what fraction of its points fall **outside the Area of Applicability** of
everything else (`frac_beyond`). This is CAST's DI/AOA logic (`trainDI`/`aoa`)
applied per component: the env-NN 95th percentile of the rest-of-data is the AOA
threshold, each held-out point's env-NN distance is its DI, and `frac_beyond` is
the share with `DI >` threshold.

- **extrapolation** (`frac_beyond ≥ extrap_frac`) — an env-distinct segment: an
  outlier population or a resolved env mode (e.g. the east outliers, the 2026
  mode). It is **kept out of training** and its points are **spread across the
  holdouts** (Steps 4–5), so no single fold absorbs a whole env-distinct lump.
- **splittable** (`n ≥ min_split_n`, not extrap) — large enough to cut: Step 4
  takes a representative test subset, Step 5 re-represents it across folds.
- **atomic** (the rest) — env-redundant small units, held out whole as filler.

`frac_beyond` is direct and tuning-light. It cleanly separates genuine
extrapolation units (`frac_beyond` ≈ 1) from the ordinary spatial-holdout
penalty (a fraction only).

For `discovery`, every unit stays intact and the holdout atom is the
super-cluster; `projection` defers to env-space thinning.

```{r step3-splittable, eval=env_ok}
partition_splittable <- function(x, pcs, purpose, min_split_n = 12, extrap_frac = 0.8) {
  xd    <- sf::st_drop_geometry(x)
  comps <- levels(x$component)
  P     <- as.matrix(xd[pcs])
  sizes <- count(xd, component, name = "n")

  # REALIZED extrapolation flag (shared by Steps 4-5): CAST's DI/AOA per component. Hold each
  # component out WHOLE; the env-NN p95 of the rest-of-data is the AOA threshold (`thr`), each
  # held-out point's env-NN distance is its DI (`enn`), and frac_beyond is the share outside
  # the AOA (DI > thr). frac_beyond ~1 ⇒ an env-distinct segment (an outlier population or a
  # resolved mode); a fraction only means a self-exclusion gap. Direct and tuning-light, and it
  # drives allocation in Steps 4-5: extrap segments are kept out of training and spread across
  # the holdouts. (trainDI()/aoa() give the same DI/threshold for a global cross-check.)
  seg_extrap <- purrr::map_dfr(comps, function(cmp) {
    te <- P[xd$component == cmp, , drop = FALSE]
    tr <- P[xd$component != cmp, , drop = FALSE]
    tnn <- c(FNN::knn.dist(tr, k = 1))                             # rest-of-data sample-to-sample NN
    thr <- stats::quantile(tnn, 0.95)                             # AOA threshold
    enn <- c(FNN::knnx.dist(data = tr, query = te, k = 1))         # held-out component's DI
    tibble(component = cmp, n_beyond = sum(enn > thr), frac_beyond = mean(enn > thr))
  })

  distinct(xd, component, supercluster) |>
    left_join(sizes,      by = "component") |>
    left_join(seg_extrap, by = "component") |>
    mutate(
      extrap     = purpose == "mapping" & frac_beyond >= extrap_frac,
      splittable = purpose == "mapping" & !extrap & n >= min_split_n,
      role = dplyr::case_when(
        purpose == "discovery"  ~ "atomic (supercluster = unit)",
        purpose == "projection" ~ "defer to env thinning",
        extrap                  ~ "extrapolation (spread, held from training)",
        splittable              ~ "splittable (interpolation)",
        TRUE                    ~ "atomic (interpolation)"))
}

spl <- partition_splittable(pts, pcs, params_part$purpose,
                            params_part$min_split_n, params_part$extrap_frac)
cat("purpose =", params_part$purpose, "| role counts:\n"); print(table(spl$role))
arrange(spl, desc(n))
```

```{r step3-plot, eval=env_ok}
med_role <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(component, supercluster) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(pcs), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(spl, component, role), by = "component")

# env-space: which components are extrapolation / splittable / atomic
ggplot(med_role, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = role, size = n)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .8) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = component), size = 2.2, max.overlaps = 40,
                           show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 10)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Step 3 — splittability in env space (purpose = %s)", params_part$purpose),
       subtitle = "size = n presences") +
  theme_minimal()

# geography: where the roles fall
pts_role <- left_join(pts, select(spl, component, role), by = "component")
ggplot(pts_role) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = role), size = 1.4, alpha = .8) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = "Step 3 — component roles on the map") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Step 4 — Test/train split (soft 70–80 %, NNDM coverage check)

`purpose = "mapping"`. The Step-3 roles drive a simple allocation:

1. **extrapolation -> spread**: a representative `test_frac` slice of the flagged
   points (k-means-medoid picks) goes to test; the rest stay in train, so Step 5's
   folds still have extrapolation to spread.
2. **splittable -> cut**: within each component, take a k-means-medoid test subset
   — cluster in env space into `n_test` groups, take the point nearest each centre.
   The picks are representative, not extreme, so both sets span the mode and test
   stays in-distribution.
3. **atomic -> whole-unit filler, hardest first**: held out intact to top up the
   test set toward the budget, hardest units (most points beyond rest-of-data p95)
   first, so the residual budget is spent deliberately.

The train proportion is a **soft target**. Test fills from (1) and (2), then
whole atomics are added greedily until the achieved proportion lands in
`train_target`.

Coverage is **measured against the training set's own structure** (the NNDM idea
from the CAST vignette): compare each test point's nearest env distance to *train*
(geodist's `test-to-sample`) against the train-to-train `sample-to-sample`
distribution. Where the two track, the
test is representative — interpolation. We **report** the tail (fraction beyond
the train-NN p95 and max) rather than forbid it; because extrap points are in
test, that tail is real and deliberate. A true `geodist`-style sample-to-
prediction comparison still needs the prediction grid and runs on the data
machine.

```{r step4-split, eval=env_ok}
partition_split <- function(x, spl, pcs, train_target, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  xd <- st_drop_geometry(x) |>
    left_join(select(spl, component, role, extrap, n_beyond), by = "component")
  N  <- nrow(xd)
  test_frac   <- 1 - mean(train_target)
  target_test <- round(N * test_frac)

  # k-means-medoid sampler: representative (not extreme) spread over all env axes
  kmed_pick <- function(M, n_pick) {
    n <- nrow(M)
    if (n_pick >= n) return(seq_len(n))
    if (n_pick < 1)  return(integer(0))
    n_pick <- min(n_pick, nrow(unique(M)))     # kmeans needs centers <= distinct points
    km <- suppressWarnings(stats::kmeans(M, centers = n_pick, nstart = 5, iter.max = 50))
    vapply(seq_len(n_pick), function(k) {
      idx <- which(km$cluster == k)
      idx[which.min(rowSums((M[idx, , drop = FALSE] -
                             matrix(km$centers[k, ], length(idx), ncol(M), byrow = TRUE))^2))]
    }, integer(1))
  }

  test_id <- integer(0)

  # 1. extrapolation segments: SPREAD their points — a representative test_frac slice to the
  #    stringent test, the rest stay in TRAIN so Step 5's inner folds have extrapolation to
  #    spread too. Env-distinct points are never dumped wholesale to either side.
  ex_ids <- xd$.id[xd$extrap]
  if (length(ex_ids)) {
    M <- as.matrix(xd[match(ex_ids, xd$.id), pcs])
    test_id <- c(test_id, ex_ids[kmed_pick(M, round(length(ex_ids) * test_frac))])
  }

  # 2. interpolation splittable: within-component representative test subset
  for (cmp in spl$component[spl$role == "splittable (interpolation)"]) {
    idx  <- xd$.id[xd$component == cmp]
    M    <- as.matrix(xd[match(idx, xd$.id), pcs])
    pick <- idx[kmed_pick(M, round(length(idx) * test_frac))]
    test_id <- c(test_id, pick)
  }

  # 3. interpolation atomic: add whole units until the budget is met, HARDEST first (most
  #    points beyond rest-of-data p95), so the residual budget is spent deliberately rather
  #    than by luck of a random draw.
  atomic_order <- spl |>
    filter(role == "atomic (interpolation)") |>
    arrange(desc(n_beyond)) |>
    pull(component)
  for (cmp in atomic_order) {
    if (length(test_id) >= target_test) break
    test_id <- c(test_id, xd$.id[xd$component == cmp])
  }

  train_id <- setdiff(xd$.id, test_id)

  # NNDM-style coverage: test->train NN env distances vs train->train NN distances
  Ptr <- as.matrix(xd[match(train_id, xd$.id), pcs])
  Pte <- as.matrix(xd[match(test_id,  xd$.id), pcs])
  test_nn  <- c(FNN::knnx.dist(data = Ptr, query = Pte, k = 1))   # test-to-sample NN
  train_nn <- c(FNN::knn.dist(Ptr, k = 1))                        # sample-to-sample LOO NN

  by_unit <- xd |>
    mutate(set = if_else(.id %in% test_id, "test", "train")) |>
    count(component, role, set) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    mutate(across(any_of(c("train", "test")), as.integer))

  list(
    train_id = train_id, test_id = test_id, by_unit = by_unit,
    achieved_train_prop = length(train_id) / N, target_test = target_test,
    nn = list(train = train_nn, test = test_nn),
    coverage = list(
      frac_beyond_p95 = mean(test_nn > stats::quantile(train_nn, 0.95)),
      frac_beyond_max = mean(test_nn > max(train_nn)))
  )
}

split <- partition_split(pts, spl, pcs, params_part$train_target, seed = params_part$seed)

cat(sprintf("train prop achieved: %.3f (target %.2f-%.2f); test n = %d (target ~%d)\n",
            split$achieved_train_prop, params_part$train_target[1], params_part$train_target[2],
            length(split$test_id), split$target_test))
cat(sprintf("NNDM coverage: %.1f%% of test beyond train-NN p95; %.1f%% beyond train-NN max\n",
            100 * split$coverage$frac_beyond_p95, 100 * split$coverage$frac_beyond_max))
split$by_unit
```

## Step 5 — CV folds (same logic, every unit out ≥ 1)

Folds are built over the **training set** (Step 4's `train_id`) — the inner CV
nested inside the outer test holdout. `k` folds, so each fold validates ~1/k
of training. The Step-3 roles drive assignment:

- **splittable -> re-represented**: k-means the component into k groups, one per
  fold, so each fold validates ~1/k of it and trains on the rest.
- **atomic -> whole unit to one fold**, load-balanced for even fold sizes.
- **extrapolation -> spread, validation-only**: flagged points are dealt
  round-robin across folds but **excluded from every fold's training**. Each
  fold gets a comparable slice of genuinely-unseen points, instead of one fold
  absorbing a whole env-distinct segment.

Output mirrors `CAST::knndm()` (`indx_train` / `indx_test`, positional row indices
into the training frame), so `modeller()`'s `trainControl(index = ...)` consumes
it unchanged.

```{r step5-folds, eval=env_ok}
# Gj / Gjstar / Gij / W via the same FNN + twosamples::wass_stat calls knndm uses internally
# (so these are the canonical knndm quantities, not a parallel computation). Gij is proxied by
# Gj off the data machine (no prediction grid); W = twosamples::wass_stat(Gjstar, Gij).
partition_knndm_dists <- function(P, clusters, extrap) {
  Gj     <- c(FNN::knn.dist(P, k = 1))                 # sample-to-sample LOO NN
  Gjstar <- numeric(nrow(P))                           # CV NN: point -> its fold's training set
  for (f in sort(unique(clusters))) {
    te <- which(clusters == f); tr <- which(clusters != f & !extrap)
    Gjstar[te] <- c(FNN::knnx.dist(data = P[tr, , drop = FALSE], query = P[te, , drop = FALSE], k = 1))
  }
  Gij <- Gj
  list(Gj = Gj, Gjstar = Gjstar, Gij = Gij, W = twosamples::wass_stat(Gjstar, Gij))
}

partition_folds <- function(x, spl, pcs, train_id, k = 10, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  xt <- st_drop_geometry(x) |> filter(.id %in% train_id) |>
    left_join(select(spl, component, role, extrap), by = "component")
  xt$row <- seq_len(nrow(xt))                       # positional index into the training frame
  k <- as.integer(k)
  fold <- integer(nrow(xt))

  # interpolation splittable: spread each component's points across the k folds (re-represent)
  for (cmp in unique(xt$component[!xt$extrap & xt$role == "splittable (interpolation)"])) {
    idx <- which(xt$component == cmp & !xt$extrap)
    M   <- as.matrix(xt[idx, pcs])
    kk  <- min(k, nrow(unique(M)))            # cap at distinct env points
    cl  <- if (kk <= 1)          rep(1L, length(idx))
           else if (kk >= nrow(M)) seq_len(nrow(M))   # each point its own cluster (avoids kmeans centers==nrow edge)
           else suppressWarnings(stats::kmeans(M, centers = kk, nstart = 5, iter.max = 50)$cluster)
    fold[idx] <- ((cl - 1) %% k) + 1
  }

  # interpolation atomic: whole unit -> one fold, greedily load-balanced
  whole <- xt |> filter(!extrap, role != "splittable (interpolation)") |>
    count(component, name = "n") |> arrange(desc(n))
  load  <- tabulate(fold[fold > 0], nbins = k)
  for (cmp in whole$component) {
    f <- which.min(load); idx <- which(xt$component == cmp & !xt$extrap)
    fold[idx] <- f; load[f] <- load[f] + length(idx)
  }

  # extrapolation points: round-robin across folds as VALIDATION-ONLY. They are given a
  # validation fold but are excluded from every fold's training (below), so each fold gets a
  # comparable slice of genuinely-unseen points instead of one fold absorbing a whole segment.
  eload <- integer(k)
  for (i in which(xt$extrap)) { f <- which.min(eload); fold[i] <- f; eload[f] <- eload[f] + 1 }

  # CAST triple: indx_train / indx_test / indx_exclude (the nndm vocabulary). Training EXCLUDES
  # all extrap rows; validation = fold members (incl the extrap dealt there); indx_exclude[[f]]
  # = extrap rows assigned to OTHER folds — neither trained nor validated in fold f.
  indx_test    <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold == f])
  indx_train   <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold != f & !xt$extrap])
  indx_exclude <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold != f &  xt$extrap])

  fold_meta <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(k), function(f) {
    in_val <- fold == f                      # bind before tibble() (a `fold` column would shadow it)
    tr <- as.matrix(xt[fold != f & !xt$extrap, pcs]); te <- as.matrix(xt[in_val, pcs])
    tnn <- c(FNN::knn.dist(tr, k = 1))                          # fold-train sample-to-sample NN
    enn <- c(FNN::knnx.dist(data = tr, query = te, k = 1))      # CV-distances (validation -> fold-train)
    tibble(fold = f, n_val = nrow(te), val_prop = nrow(te) / nrow(xt),
           n_extrap_val = sum(xt$extrap[in_val]),
           beyond_p95 = mean(enn > stats::quantile(tnn, 0.95)),
           beyond_max = mean(enn > max(tnn)))
  })

  # knndm-canonical, classed object: same field names as CAST::knndm, so CAST::print.knndm and
  # CAST::plot.knndm work on it directly (we maintain no print/plot code). Extra fields (clusters
  # is id-keyed via `fold`, plus indx_exclude/extrap_id/fold_meta/role) ride alongside harmlessly.
  d <- partition_knndm_dists(as.matrix(xt[pcs]), fold, xt$extrap)
  res <- list(
    clusters   = fold,                                  # per-training-row fold id (knndm$clusters)
    indx_train = indx_train, indx_test = indx_test, indx_exclude = indx_exclude,
    Gij = d$Gij, Gj = d$Gj, Gjstar = d$Gjstar, W = d$W,
    method = "single-linkage graph", q = "role-based (cut/re-represent/spread)",
    space = "feature", dist_space = "feature",
    k = k, fold = setNames(fold, xt$.id), extrap_id = xt$.id[xt$extrap], fold_meta = fold_meta)
  class(res) <- c("knndm", "list")
  res
}

folds <- partition_folds(pts, spl, pcs, split$train_id, params_part$k,
                         seed = params_part$seed)
cat(sprintf("k = %d folds over %d training points; every unit held out >= 1.\n",
            folds$k, length(split$train_id)))
folds$fold_meta
```

`knndm()` picks folds by minimising **`W`**, the Wasserstein distance between the
CV nearest-neighbour distances (`Gjstar`) and the prediction NN distances
(`Gij`). We don't run `knndm()`'s fold search, but `partition_folds()` now carries
the same `Gj`/`Gjstar`/`Gij`/`W` fields and is classed `c("knndm", "list")`, so
`W` is the single number that answers the "coverage objective" open question and
lets Step 5 and Step 5b be compared — and **CAST's own `print.knndm`/`plot.knndm`
render it**, so we maintain no reporting code. `Gjstar` is each training point's
env-NN to its fold's *training* set; `Gij` is proxied by the sample-to-sample LOO
env-NN (`Gj`) until the data-machine prediction grid is available. Lower `W` ⇒
folds reproduce the reference NN-distance structure better.

```{r step5-W, eval=env_ok}
print(folds)                                 # CAST::print.knndm, dispatched on our object
plot(folds, stat = "ecdf", type = "simple")  # CAST::plot.knndm (Gij curve == Gj until the grid)
```

  mutate(fold = factor(folds$fold[as.character(.id)]))

ggplot(fold_pts) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = fold), size = 1.3, alpha = .85) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Step 5 — %d CV folds on the training set (validation fold per point)", folds$k)) +
  theme_minimal()

folds$fold_meta |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(fold), beyond_p95, fill = n_extrap_val)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_point(aes(y = beyond_max), colour = "black", size = 2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(title = "Step 5 — per-fold extrapolation content (spread evenly)",
       subtitle = "bar = beyond train-NN p95; black point = beyond train-NN max",
       x = "fold", y = "fraction of validation beyond train-NN", fill = "extrap pts") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Step 5b (dev) — Segment-LOPO folds (knock out whole segments)

A **leave-whole-segment-out** alternative to Step 5, for mapping suitable habitat
in the current domain — the Pili "LOPO sense" on our graph. Interpolation
segments are held out **whole** (not re-represented): each component goes intact
into one fold, grouped by greedy **size-balancing** so fold sizes stay even.
Extrapolation points are spread across folds validation-only, exactly as in Step
5. Drop-in with Step 5: same output shape, run over the Step-4 training set.

The point is the **env coverage per fold** (same NNDM lens). Within the massif
env ⊥ geo, so pulling a whole local segment still leaves its *environment*
bracketed by the segments that remain — most folds stay interpolation
(beyond-max ≈ 0), a legitimate mapping evaluation. The folds with a high
`beyond_p95` are the honest whole-segment gaps, flagged so they can be read
apart from the interpolation bulk.

```{r step5b-lopo, eval=env_ok}
partition_folds_lopo <- function(x, spl, pcs, train_id, k = 10, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  xt <- st_drop_geometry(x) |> filter(.id %in% train_id) |>
    left_join(select(spl, component, role, extrap), by = "component")
  xt$row <- seq_len(nrow(xt))                    # positional index into the training frame
  k <- as.integer(k)
  fold <- integer(nrow(xt))

  # interpolation segments: whole segment -> one fold, greedy size-balance (true leave-segment-out)
  csz  <- xt |> filter(!extrap) |> count(component, name = "n") |> arrange(desc(n))
  load <- integer(k)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(csz))) {
    f <- which.min(load); idx <- which(xt$component == csz$component[i] & !xt$extrap)
    fold[idx] <- f; load[f] <- load[f] + csz$n[i]
  }

  # extrapolation points: round-robin across folds as VALIDATION-ONLY (excluded from training
  # below), so every fold gets a comparable slice of genuinely-unseen points.
  eload <- integer(k)
  for (i in which(xt$extrap)) { f <- which.min(eload); fold[i] <- f; eload[f] <- eload[f] + 1 }

  # CAST triple (nndm vocabulary): training EXCLUDES all extrap rows; validation = fold members
  # (whole interp segment + extrap dealt there); indx_exclude[[f]] = extrap rows of OTHER folds.
  indx_test    <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold == f])
  indx_train   <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold != f & !xt$extrap])
  indx_exclude <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) xt$row[fold != f &  xt$extrap])

  fold_meta <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(k), function(f) {
    in_val <- fold == f                          # bind before tibble() (a `fold` column would shadow it)
    tr <- as.matrix(xt[fold != f & !xt$extrap, pcs]); te <- as.matrix(xt[in_val, pcs])
    tnn <- c(FNN::knn.dist(tr, k = 1))                          # fold-train sample-to-sample NN
    enn <- c(FNN::knnx.dist(data = tr, query = te, k = 1))      # CV-distances (validation -> fold-train)
    tibble(fold = f, n_val = nrow(te), val_prop = nrow(te) / nrow(xt),
           n_comp = dplyr::n_distinct(xt$component[in_val & !xt$extrap]),
           n_superc = dplyr::n_distinct(xt$supercluster[in_val]),
           n_extrap_val = sum(xt$extrap[in_val]),
           beyond_p95 = mean(enn > stats::quantile(tnn, 0.95)),
           beyond_max = mean(enn > max(tnn)))
  })

  # knndm-canonical classed object (same as partition_folds), so CAST's print/plot dispatch here too
  d <- partition_knndm_dists(as.matrix(xt[pcs]), fold, xt$extrap)
  res <- list(
    clusters   = fold,
    indx_train = indx_train, indx_test = indx_test, indx_exclude = indx_exclude,
    Gij = d$Gij, Gj = d$Gj, Gjstar = d$Gjstar, W = d$W,
    method = "segment-LOPO (whole segment)", q = "leave-segment-out",
    space = "feature", dist_space = "feature",
    k = k, fold = setNames(fold, xt$.id), extrap_id = xt$.id[xt$extrap], fold_meta = fold_meta)
  class(res) <- c("knndm", "list")
  res
}

folds_lopo <- partition_folds_lopo(pts, spl, pcs, split$train_id, params_part$k,
                                   seed = params_part$seed)
cat(sprintf("segment-LOPO: k = %d folds over %d training points; %d whole segments, each out once.\n",
            folds_lopo$k, length(split$train_id), length(unique(folds_lopo$clusters))))
cat(sprintf("mean beyond-p95 = %.1f%%, mean beyond-max = %.1f%% (env cost of leaving whole segments out)\n",
            100 * mean(folds_lopo$fold_meta$beyond_p95),
            100 * mean(folds_lopo$fold_meta$beyond_max)))

# W now rides inside each fold object, so the two schemes compare on one number
cat(sprintf("W: Step 5b segment-LOPO = %.3f vs Step 5 CV folds = %.3f (lower reproduces NN structure better)\n",
            folds_lopo$W, folds$W))
folds_lopo$fold_meta
```

# (3) CB + Cochetopa per fold — rows: region (Cochetopa second), columns: fold;
#     held-out segment red; Step-4 test holdout as blue crosses in every panel.
assign_region <- function(sfobj) {                       # region from lon/lat (data is UTM 13N)
  ll <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sfobj, 4326))
  sfobj |> st_drop_geometry() |>
    mutate(lon = ll[, 1], lat = ll[, 2],
           region = dplyr::case_when(
             lat < 38.5                 ~ "Cochetopa",
             lat > 38.85 & lon < -106.9 ~ "CB",
             TRUE                       ~ "other")) |>
    filter(region %in% c("CB", "Cochetopa")) |>
    mutate(region = factor(region, levels = c("CB", "Cochetopa")))   # CB top, Cochetopa second
}

                                   TRUE             ~ "in train"))

  geom_point(aes(colour = status), size = .8, alpha = .85) +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(grid, status == "extrap (held out)"),
             shape = 2, colour = "black", size = 1.4, stroke = .5) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = c("segment held out" = "firebrick",

  facet_grid(region ~ panel_fold, switch = "y", scales = "free", space = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Step 5b — CB and Cochetopa by fold (red = segment; △ = spread extrap; blue × = test)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
```

## Step 6 — Class-aware assembly (presences + absences → one caret-ready frame)

Presences keep the structured partition from Steps 4–5. **Absences do not form
populations to hold out, so they are randomly sampled** — a random outer split at
the same proportion, then balanced random folds. Random still keeps ~`(k-1)/k` of
absences in every fold's training and preserves the presence:absence ratio in
each set.

> **On the data machine:** the proper Option-A flow regenerates the env-distance
> PA pool *against the outer-train presences only* after the presence split, then
> feeds it here. Without rasters, we use the existing pool (`bg`,
> `iter1-pa.gpkg`); the assignment logic is identical (random), only the PA
> provenance differs. Absences need no env here — predictors are attached at fit
> time.

```{r step6-classes, eval=env_ok}
partition_classes <- function(pts, bg, split, folds, train_target, k, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  test_prop <- 1 - mean(train_target)

  # presences: structured assignment from Steps 4-5 (test presences get fold = NA).
  # extrap presences carry their validation fold but are flagged so they are NEVER put in
  # any fold's training (they are validation-only, matching the Step 5 spread).
  pres <- tibble(
    id     = paste0("pres_", pts$.id),
    class  = 1L,
    set    = if_else(pts$.id %in% split$test_id, "test", "train"),
    fold   = unname(folds$fold[as.character(pts$.id)]),
    extrap = pts$.id %in% folds$extrap_id)

  # absences: random outer split, then balanced random folds within the train side
  nb  <- nrow(bg)
  aid <- paste0("abs_", seq_len(nb))
  a_set <- rep("train", nb); a_set[sample.int(nb, round(nb * test_prop))] <- "test"
  a_fold <- rep(NA_integer_, nb)
  tr <- which(a_set == "train")
  a_fold[tr] <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(tr)))      # balanced across folds
  abs <- tibble(id = aid, class = 0L, set = a_set, fold = a_fold, extrap = FALSE)

  combined <- bind_rows(pres, abs)
  tf <- combined[combined$set == "train", ]; tf$row <- seq_len(nrow(tf))
  # CAST triple (nndm vocabulary) carried through to the caret-ready frame.
  indx_test    <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) tf$row[which(tf$fold == f)])
  indx_train   <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) tf$row[which(tf$fold != f & !tf$extrap)])
  indx_exclude <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(f) tf$row[which(tf$fold != f &  tf$extrap)])

  list(combined = combined, train_frame = tf,
       indx_train = indx_train, indx_test = indx_test, indx_exclude = indx_exclude,
       test_ids = combined$id[combined$set == "test"])
}

classes <- partition_classes(pts, bg, split, folds, params_part$train_target,
                             params_part$k, seed = params_part$seed)

# class balance per set, and presence:absence ratio
classes$combined |>
  count(set, class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(absence = `0`, presence = `1`) |>
  mutate(ratio_abs_per_pres = round(absence / presence, 2))
```

```{r step6-foldbalance, eval=env_ok}
# per-fold class balance in the combined training frame (what caret will tune on)
classes$train_frame |>
  filter(!is.na(fold)) |>
  count(fold, class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(absence = `0`, presence = `1`) |>
  mutate(n_val = absence + presence, pres_frac = round(presence / n_val, 2))
```

## Assemble — `build_partition()`

One function composes Steps 1–6 into the single artifact downstream code reads.
Its shape mirrors `spatial_class_split()` + `knndm()`, so `modeller(split = ...)`
and `trainControl(index = ...)` both work. It subsumes LOPO (populations =
components), edist folds (cut within env-homogeneous components), and the
extrapolation audit in one object.

`x` already carries the PCA columns (Step 0) and `pcs` names them; `bg` is the
absence set.

```{r build-partition, eval=env_ok}
build_partition <- function(x, bg, pcs, p) {   # p = params_part
  x     <- partition_components(x, p$connect_m)
  geo_d <- partition_geo_dist(x)
  x$supercluster <- factor(
    cutree(hclust(as.dist(geo_d), method = "single"), h = p$superclust_m)[as.character(x$component)])
  env_d   <- partition_env_dist(x, pcs)
  spl     <- partition_splittable(x, pcs, p$purpose, p$min_split_n, p$extrap_frac)
  split   <- partition_split(x, spl, pcs, p$train_target, p$seed)
  folds   <- partition_folds(x, spl, pcs, split$train_id, p$k, p$seed)
  classes <- partition_classes(x, bg, split, folds, p$train_target, p$k, p$seed)

  list(
    # presence-level structure
    train_id   = split$train_id,
    test_id    = split$test_id,
    components = select(st_drop_geometry(x), .id, component, supercluster),
    geo_d = geo_d, env_d = env_d, splittable = spl,
    split_coverage = split$coverage, fold_meta = folds$fold_meta, W = folds$W,
    folds = folds,                        # the classed knndm object (CAST print/plot dispatch)
    # class-aware frame for fitting (caret-ready)
    combined   = classes$combined,        # every point: id, class, set, fold
    train_frame = classes$train_frame,
    indx_train   = classes$indx_train,    # positional into train_frame, for caret::trainControl(index=)
    indx_test    = classes$indx_test,     # ...and indexOut=
    indx_exclude = classes$indx_exclude,  # nndm-style: held from training, not validated (extrap)
    test_ids     = classes$test_ids,
    meta = p[c("connect_m", "superclust_m", "train_target", "k", "purpose",
               "pca_var_target", "min_split_n", "extrap_frac", "seed")]
  )
}

# single-call check: reproduces the inline Steps 1-6 and returns the caret-ready object.
# extrap rows are validation-only: each is validated once but NEVER trained, so it lands in
# indx_test once, indx_exclude k-1 times, and indx_train zero times; everyone else trains k-1
# times and validates once. This is exactly the nndm indx_train/indx_test/indx_exclude split.
part <- build_partition(pts, bg, pcs, params_part)
ntr  <- nrow(part$train_frame)
is_ex <- part$train_frame$extrap
tr_count <- tabulate(unlist(part$indx_train),   nbins = ntr)
ex_count <- tabulate(unlist(part$indx_exclude), nbins = ntr)
stopifnot(
  identical(sort(part$train_id), sort(split$train_id)),            # same presence split
  all(tabulate(unlist(part$indx_test), nbins = ntr) == 1),         # each train row validated once
  all(tr_count[!is_ex] == params_part$k - 1),                      # non-extrap trained k-1 times
  all(tr_count[is_ex]  == 0),                                      # extrap never trained
  all(ex_count[is_ex]  == params_part$k - 1),                      # extrap excluded from the k-1 other folds
  all(ex_count[!is_ex] == 0)                                       # non-extrap never excluded
)
cat(sprintf("build_partition() OK: %d train / %d test presences (%d extrap held from training); %d-row frame; %d folds; %d test ids.\n",
            length(part$train_id), length(part$test_id), sum(is_ex), ntr,
            length(part$indx_train), length(part$test_ids)))
part$combined |> count(set, class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(absence = `0`, presence = `1`)
```

## Open questions carried forward

- **`connect_m` derivation** — formalise the variogram-range / geodist-knee
  choice; sensitivity-test across resolutions.
- **`extrap_frac` sensitivity** — how many segments the flag catches, and the
  train/test extrap split, across thresholds.
- **The objective** (Steps 4–5) — now reported as `knndm()`'s `W` (Wasserstein
  `Gjstar` vs `Gij`); on the data machine swap the `Gj` proxy for the true
  prediction-grid `Gij` so `W` balances "test looks like prediction" against
  "train covers test" exactly as `knndm()` does.
- **Wire into `modeller()`** — feed `indx_train`/`indx_test` to `trainControl()`
  (`indx_exclude` is already dropped from `indx_train`); decide whether mapping
  uses Step 5 or the Step 5b folds — compare them on `W`.
